verses: ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ٱكْتَالُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ
كَلَّآ إِنَّ كِتَٰبَ ٱلْفُجَّارِ لَفِى سِجِّينٍ
وَمَا يُكَذِّبُ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ
إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
كَلَّا بَلْ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
كَلَّآ إِنَّهُمْ عَن رَّبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّمَحْجُوبُونَ
ثُمَّ يُقَالُ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
كَلَّآ إِنَّ كِتَٰبَ ٱلْأَبْرَارِ لَفِى عِلِّيِّينَ
خِتَٰمُهُۥ مِسْكٌ وَفِى ذَٰلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ ٱلْمُتَنَٰفِسُونَ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا۟ كَانُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ يَضْحَكُونَ
وَإِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِمُ ٱنقَلَبُوا۟ فَكِهِينَ
وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ لَضَآلُّونَ
فَٱلْيَوْمَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ
هَلْ ثُوِّبَ ٱلْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْعَلُونَ

leads.title: The basket of summer fruit; cheating merchants; famine of the word ↔ The defrauders: Sijjin and 'Illiyyun
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded (weight 4.7). Pair score 4.7.

Only in The basket of summer fruit; cheating merchants; famine of the word: Vision of a basket of summer fruit (qayits) means 'the end (qets) has come'; A famine not of bread or thirst for water, but of hearing the words of YHWH; they wander from sea to sea seeking it; Those who swear by the Ashimah of Samaria, 'As your god lives, O Dan', and 'As the way of Beersheba lives'; God will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight; The whole land heaves and sinks like the Nile of Egypt; Merchants ask when the new moon and sabbath will be over so they can sell grain with small ephah, big shekel and false scales; God will make it like the mourning for an only son, with sackcloth and baldness; They sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals; God asks the prophet 'What do you see?' and interprets the ordinary object he names.

Only in The defrauders: Sijjin and 'Illiyyun: Woe to the defrauders (mutaffifin) who exact full measure from others but give short measure or weight; The record of the wicked is in Sijjin, that of the righteous in 'Illiyyun, each an inscribed book (kitab marqum) witnessed by those brought near; Sinners laughed at and winked at believers; on that day the believers laugh at the unbelievers from their couches; What they earned has covered their hearts with rust (rana); Deniers dismiss the recited signs as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin); On that day the wicked are veiled (debarred) from their Lord; An elite of 'those brought near' (al-muqarrabun) witness the righteous register and drink from Tasnim; A merchant (Canaan) with false scales in his hand loves to oppress; The record of the wicked is in Sijjin, that of the righteous in 'Illiyyun, each an inscribed book (kitab marqum) witnessed by those brought near [divergence between the texts]; The righteous drink sealed pure wine (rahiq makhtum) whose seal is musk; Paradise has named springs: Salsabil, Tasnim (and a spring the servants of God make gush forth); Paradise has raised couches (arā'ik, surur), set goblets, cushions in rows and spread carpets; and 4 more.
